chunks: If you endure with the endurance of the noble/generous ones, or else you will forget/behave with the forgetting/behavior of the beasts.

key_terms.الْأَكَارِمِ: The noble, the generous, the high-born
key_terms.سَلَوْتَ: You forgot, you became heedless, or you behaved

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between enduring grief like a noble person versus an animal according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali contrasts the conscious, dignified patience of the noble (al-akaram) with the heedless, passive oblivion of beasts (al-bahaim), emphasizing that true resilience requires active spiritual awareness rather than mere endurance. This dichotomy reflects the Shia ethical ideal of maintaining human distinctiveness through mindful composure in adversity. The phrase serves as a practical guide for believers to elevate their grief from mere suffering to a state of noble fortitude.
